newsitem.title: USA: Revco launches offer for Big B.
newsitem.headline: Revco launches offer for Big B.

text.p: Revco D.S. Inc., the nation's second-largest drugstore chain, Monday launched an unsolicited cash tender offer worth $330 million for the remaining stock of Big B Inc. that it does not already own.

The offer followed an announcement by Phar-Mor Inc. and ShopKo Inc. that they agreed to merge into a new drugstore holding company with combined annual sales of about $3.2 billion from 232 stores in 29 states.
Revco, which owns 5.4 percent or 1,190,000 of Big B's 22 million common shares outstanding, said it launched the $15 per share tender offer after the company rejected its friendly proposal.

The offer, which expires Oct. 7, represents a premium of 53 percent over the $9.81 average closing price of Bessemer, Ala.-based Big B's stock for the 90-calendar day period ended Friday. The stock soared $3 to $15.625 on Nasdaq at mid-morning.
Revco rose 25 cents to $25.875 on the New York Stock Exchange.
Twinsburg, Ohio-based Revco said it expects the deal to enhance its earnings per share in the first year after the merger.
Revco said it intends to finance the tender offer through a combination of cash on hand and bank borrowings.
The offer is conditioned on the acquisition of a majority of Big B's shares on a fully diluted basis and antitrust approval by regulators, Revco said.

D. Dwayne Hoven, Revco's president and CEO, said in a letter dated Sept. 9 to Big B that the companies represent an excellent geographic fit, with only limited overlap of stores and distribution centres.

"Among other efficiencies, this combination will allow the combined company to spread costs over a larger base of stores. This will assist us in meeting the increasing customer demand for lower pharmacy prices," he said in the letter to his Big B counterpart, Anthony J. Bruno.
Big B operates 389 drug stores and nine Home Health Care stores in Alabama, Florida, Georgia, Mississippi and Tennessee.
Revco operates 2,184 stores in 14 contiguous Midwestern, Southeastern and Eastern states. It has more than 32,000 employees.
